porbos.title: Whose House Did the Prophet ﷺ Stay In • Who Had Tubba‘’s Poem • A City, Not Yet a State • The Call No One Had Heard • Brother and Brother • The Bond of Salman and Abu al-Darda’ • Half the Wealth, Just a Road • The Date-Orchard Proposal

blocks.0: Whose House Did the Prophet ﷺ Stay In
blocks.1: There are many houses in Madinah. In whose house did the Prophet {{1}} stay? The answer came from a small question.
blocks.3: The Prophet {{1}} asked, which of our relatives’ houses is nearest? Abu Ayyub (RA) said, I am, O Prophet of Allah! This is my house, and this is my door. He said, then go and prepare a resting place for us. Abu Ayyub said, you two come up, with the blessing of Allah.{{2}}
blocks.4: The nearest house. That was the whole calculation of the choice. And the one in whose house the guest stayed did not stand at the door and say, my house is small. He said, this is my house, this is my door. With this one house the dars’s story begins.
blocks.6: An old story is joined to the house of Abu Ayyub (RA). From long before the Prophet’s {{1}} birth. A king of Yemen; Tubban As‘ad Abu Karib. Ibn Ishaq wrote about him. On his return from a war in the east he stopped at Madinah. Earlier he had come this way once and left one of his sons among them, and that son was killed in a plot. This time he came to destroy Madinah, to cut down the date palms, to wipe out the people. The Ansar were fighting that Yemeni army. In Ibn Ishaq’s narration the Ansar claim that by day they fought him, and by night they hosted him. Tubba‘ said in amazement, by Allah, our people seem to be cowards! Then two Jewish scholars of Banu Qurayzah came to him.
blocks.8: O king, do not do this. If you do what you want, a barrier will form between you and this city. He asked, why? They said, this is the place of Hijrah of a prophet; in the last age he will emerge from this sanctuary of Quraysh, and this will be his home and his dwelling place.{{1}}
blocks.9: Tubba‘ stopped. Madinah was saved. Suhayli wrote that, hearing the news of the Prophet {{1}} from the two scholars, the king recited a poem.
blocks.11: I bear witness about Ahmad that he is a messenger from Allah, the Creator of souls. If my life were extended to his life, I would be his vizier and his cousin. I would fight his enemies with the sword, and remove every worry from his chest.{{1}}
blocks.12: Suhayli also wrote that the Ansar had kept this poem, hand to hand, through the generations. And it was with Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (RA). Up to here it is in the chain. That Tubba‘ himself built Abu Ayyub’s house is something heard by word of mouth. But it is not in this chapter of Ibn Ishaq or Ibn Kathir. We do not say that here. What is in the chain is this: long before the Prophet {{1}}, a Yemeni king had heard that a prophet would come to this city. The people of this city had carried the word of that prophet in a poem. And on the day the Prophet {{2}} came, the one in whose house he stayed had that very poem.
blocks.13: A City, Not Yet a State
blocks.14: The she-camel had knelt. The mosque had risen. Salam had reached house after house. But a mosque in a city does not make it a state. In Madinah then there were three kinds of people. The Muhajirun who came from Makkah; leaving house, business, kin, everything. The old inhabitants of Yathrib, the Ansar; the land theirs, the date orchards theirs, but the old blood-accounts of Aws and Khazraj had not yet dried. And three Jewish tribes; Banu Qaynuqa‘, Banu al-Nadir, Banu Qurayzah. Their homes too were in this very city.{{1}}
blocks.15: Aws and Khazraj; living in the same city, the blood of Bu‘ath had not yet dried, this has come in dars 11 itself. The Muhajirun were guests in someone’s house, partners in someone’s orchard. No earnings of their own, no home of their own. Three kinds of people on one piece of earth. No blood relation of anyone with anyone. Not even the same religion of anyone with anyone. The Prophet’s {{1}} task then was not only to lead prayer. It was to join a city and make a state.
blocks.16: Today’s dars is the story of that joining. One call, one bond of brotherhood, and one written document; with these three a city became a state.
blocks.17: The Call No One Had Heard
blocks.18: When the time of prayer came, how to gather people? The Prophet {{1}} was thinking. Could someone be sent to call them? Raise a flag?{{2}}
blocks.19: One said, ring a bell like the Nasara. It did not please the Prophet {{1}}. Another said, blow the horn of the Jews. Not that either. That night ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd (RA) saw a dream.
blocks.21: I saw in a dream a man wearing two green cloths, in his hand a bell. I said, O servant of Allah, will you sell the bell? He said, what will you do with it? I said, call people to prayer. He said, shall I not tell you something better than this? I said, tell me. He said, say, Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar... In this way he taught the whole adhan.{{1}}
blocks.22: In the morning he rushed to the Prophet {{1}}. He told the dream.
blocks.24: The Prophet {{1}} said, this is a true dream. Go with Bilal (RA) and teach him what you heard; for his voice is louder than yours. I went with Bilal to the mosque; I would say it, and he would call out. ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) heard Bilal’s call and came out dragging his cloak, saying, O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I too saw this very same dream.{{2}}
blocks.25: One person’s dream. Another’s same dream as confirmation. The first adhan was given by Bilal (RA); who until not long before was the slave of a polytheist of Makkah, flogged for saying only ‘Ahad’. The voice that once, fallen on the desert sand, had said ‘Ahad, Ahad’, that same voice now calls the whole city from the minaret.
blocks.26: Five times a day this call is now uttered across the whole world in the same language, the same tune. This call began with a dream. And that very call is today the most often uttered of all the words of people.
blocks.28: The Muhajirun had no money in hand, no land, no business reputation. The Ansar had houses, had land, but no one had ever stood beside them in this city like the Muhajirun. The Prophet {{1}} did one thing that no society of Arabia had done before.
blocks.29: Sitting in the house of Anas ibn Malik (RA), he bound brother to brother among the Muhajirun and the Ansar.
blocks.31: ‘Asim (RA) says, I asked Anas (RA), has it reached you that the Prophet {{1}} said, there is no hilf (tribal alliance pact) in Islam? He said, the Prophet {{2}} made a bond between Quraysh and the Ansar in my very house.{{3}}
blocks.32: The question was whether the old tribal alliance pacts of Jahiliyyah would run in Islam. The answer of Anas (RA) was that the Prophet {{1}} himself had made a new bond in this very house; but not for tribal interest, on the basis of faith. Not brothers of blood. Brothers made in a night.
blocks.33: Who the bond was between, Ibn Ishaq has told name by name. The brother of Abu Bakr (RA) was Kharijah ibn Zayd (RA). The brother of ‘Umar (RA) was ‘Itban ibn Malik (RA). And the brother of ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf (RA) was Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ (RA).{{1}}
blocks.35: The Prophet {{1}} made brotherhood between Abu ‘Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah and Abu Talhah (RA).{{2}}
blocks.36: In one narration of the Sirah it is said that the Prophet {{1}} himself took ‘Ali’s (RA) hand and said, this is my brother; but the narration has no chain, Ibn Ishaq himself brought it in the language of doubt, and Ibn Kathir objected, so it is not evidence.{{2}}
blocks.37: Nearly ninety people; half Muhajirun, half Ansar. In the early days, inheritance of property also ran in this bond of brotherhood; instead of the blood relative, this new brother would get the wealth. Later it was abrogated by a verse of the Qur’an; inheritance went back to blood relations alone.{{1}}
blocks.38: But the bond remained; a bond of love, a bond of sharing wealth, a bond of the heart.
blocks.39: The Bond of Salman and Abu al-Darda’
blocks.40: Binding brothers was not only sharing wealth. For some it was a bond of keeping one another on the straight path. The Prophet {{1}} bound Salman al-Farisi (RA) as brother to Abu al-Darda’ (RA).
blocks.42: One day Salman (RA) visited the house of Abu al-Darda’ (RA). He saw Umm al-Darda’ in a dishevelled state. He asked, what is your condition? She said, your brother Abu al-Darda’ has no interest in the world. When Abu al-Darda’ came she prepared food for him; Salman said, eat. Abu al-Darda’ said, I am fasting. Salman said, I will not eat unless you eat. He ate. When night came Abu al-Darda’ went to stand in prayer. Salman said, sleep. He slept. He went to get up again; Salman again said, sleep. In the last part of the night Salman said, now get up. The two prayed. Then Salman said, your Lord has a right on you, your own body has a right on you, your family has a right on you; give each one who has a right his right. Abu al-Darda’ went to the Prophet {{1}} and told what had happened. The Prophet {{2}} said, Salman has spoken truly.{{3}}
blocks.43: One brother brought the other back from excess. And the Prophet {{1}} sealed that very turning-back as true. ‘Salman (RA) has spoken truly’; in this one sentence it is understood that in the bond of brotherhood there was also the right to correct one another.
blocks.44: Half the Wealth, Just a Road
blocks.45: Among the Muhajirun one came almost empty-handed; ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf (RA). The Prophet {{1}} bound him as brother to Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ (RA). Sa‘d was rich. Anas (RA) has told of that day.
blocks.47: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf (RA) came to Madinah. The Prophet {{1}} bound brotherhood between him and Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ al-Ansari (RA). Sa‘d was wealthy. He said to ‘Abd al-Rahman, let me divide my wealth in two with you, and I will also have you married. ‘Abd al-Rahman said, may Allah bless your family and wealth. Just show me the way to the market. He did not stop until he found the way, and at last returned with some ghee and cheese. He said, we spent some days like this, or as long as Allah willed. Then he came with a mark of yellow on his clothes. The Prophet {{2}} said, what is this? He said, O Messenger of Allah, I have married an Ansari woman. He asked, what mahr did you give? He said, gold the weight of a date stone, or a date stone of gold. The Prophet {{3}} said, hold a walimah, even with a goat.{{4}}
blocks.48: Half the wealth, a marriage proposal; the greatest gifts were set before him. ‘Abd al-Rahman (RA) took not one of them. He asked only for the road to the market. After a few days he stood on his own feet. Beginning with ghee and cheese, then his own marriage, his own walimah; all from his own earnings. Sa‘d (RA) had given just this much; showing the road. One wished to give half of the wealth. The other asked only for a place to stand.
blocks.50: Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ (RA) was not alone. One day the Ansar went in a group to the Prophet {{1}} with a proposal.
blocks.52: The Ansar said to the Prophet {{1}}, divide the date orchards between us and our brothers. He said, no. Then they said, then you (the Muhajirun) bear the labour for us, and we will make you partners in the crop. They (the Muhajirun) said, we heard and we obeyed.{{2}}
blocks.53: The Ansar had wanted to divide the very ownership of the land. The Prophet {{1}} did not agree. In its place a middle way came out. The land would remain with the Ansar. The labour the Muhajirun would give; tending the orchard, watering, gathering the crop. In return a share of the crop. Not a gift; an exchange for work. The Muhajirun have no land, true, but they have labour. That very labour was made their capital. The proposal of half the wealth by Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ (RA), and this date-orchard proposal of the Ansar; both events speak of the same nature. Before taking, keeping a road to work open.

footnotes.1: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Story of Tubba‘ Abi Karib with the people of Madinah’; from the Sirah, without a chain. So as a scene, not as evidence
footnotes.2: Suhayli ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, the same chapter; from the Sirah, without a chain; the poem is current as Tubba‘’s, not verified through an independent source
footnotes.3: The background of the three Jewish tribes settled in Madinah and their old presence: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Section on his (peace be upon him) making the bond of affection between the Muhajirun and the Ansar’ (via al-Tabari; a Sirah background).
footnotes.4: Consideration of various proposals before the adhan: Sunan Abi Dawud 499 (via Muhammad, the son of ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd (RA); the chain of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Imam al-Tirmidhi: hasan sahih); Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 189.
footnotes.5: Sunan Abi Dawud 499 (from Muhammad, the son of ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd (RA), on the authority of his father); to the same effect Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 189 (Imam al-Tirmidhi: hadithun hasanun sahih)
footnotes.6: Sunan Abi Dawud 499 (from Muhammad, the son of ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd (RA), on the authority of his father); to the same effect Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 189 (Imam al-Tirmidhi: hadithun hasanun sahih)
footnotes.7: Sahih al-Bukhari 2294 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)); to the same effect Sahih al-Bukhari 6083, 7340
footnotes.8: The name-by-name list: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Section on the Prophet’s {{1}} making brotherhood between the Muhajirun and the Ansar’ (from Ibn Ishaq). This list begins directly chainless with ‘fima balaghana’ (what has reached us); so it is from the Sirah, not every pair directly proved in hadith. Ibn Kathir himself raised some objections to it; for example, Ibn Ishaq said the pair of Abu ‘Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah (RA) was Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh (RA), whereas in Musnad Ahmad and Sahih Muslim, directly with a chain, his pair was Abu Talhah (RA) (see the next citation); Ibn Kathir said this is the more sound. The pair of ‘Abd al-Rahman (RA) and Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ (RA) is directly proved in Sahih al-Bukhari 2049.
footnotes.10: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Section on the Prophet’s {{1}} making brotherhood’; from the Sirah, without a chain. Ibn Ishaq’s words ‘fima balaghana wa na‘udhu billahi an naqula ‘alayhi ma lam yaqul’ (what has reached us, and we seek refuge in Allah from saying about him what he did not say); Ibn Kathir’s objection begins in the same chapter with the words ‘fa-fi ba‘di ma dhakarahu nazar’. As an explanation he said that ‘Ali (RA) had been under the care of the Prophet {{2}} since childhood.
footnotes.11: Abrogation of the ruling of inheritance: Sahih al-Bukhari (the tafsir of Ibn ‘Abbas (RA), in connection with Surah al-Nisa’ 4:33): when the Muhajir came to Madinah, the Ansari bound as brother, instead of the blood relative, would receive the inheritance; when ‘the blood relatives are more entitled to one another in Allah’s ruling’ in Surah al-Anfal 75 was revealed, this ruling was cancelled. In this dars it has not been discussed in detail; only the event.

quiz.q: What are the names of the three Jewish tribes settled in Madinah?
o: Banu Qaynuqa‘, Banu al-Nadir
Banu Aws, Banu Khazraj, Banu Najjar
Banu ‘Awf, Banu al-Harith, Banu Sa‘idah
Banu Jahsh, Banu ‘Adi, Banu Umayyah
quiz.e: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah.

quiz.q: What task did the presence of the three parties in Madinah, Muhajirun, Ansar and Jews, put before the Prophet ﷺ?
o: Not only leading prayer
Only completing the building of the mosque
Only bringing unity among the Ansar
Only removing the Jews from Madinah
quiz.e: People different in tribe and religion had to be joined in one city.

quiz.q: Which two proposals did the Prophet ﷺ not accept for announcing the time of prayer?
o: Raising a flag and beating a drum
A bell like the Nasara
Lighting a fire and raising smoke
Sending someone to call, and writing a letter
quiz.e: Sunan Abi Dawud 499.

quiz.q: How did the words of the adhan reach the Prophet ﷺ?
o: Jibril (AS) came directly and taught them
Bilal (RA) composed them himself
In the dream of ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd (RA)
The words of the adhan were revealed directly in a verse of the Qur’an
quiz.e: Sunan Abi Dawud 499; Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 189 (hasan sahih).

quiz.q: Who gave the first adhan?
o: ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd (RA), who saw the dream
‘Umar (RA), who saw the same dream
Abu Bakr (RA), who led the first prayer
Bilal (RA)
quiz.e: Because his voice was the loudest.

quiz.q: From the proposal of a bell or horn for the adhan, why does it seem the Prophet ﷺ did not accept it?
o: Because they were hard to make
Because they were symbols of other religions
Because their sound was not loud enough
Because they were expensive
quiz.e: They are mentioned as the signs of the Nasara and the Jews.

quiz.q: How does ‘Umar’s (RA) seeing the same dream make the dream of ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd (RA) important?
o: It shows the dream was wrong
It reduces Bilal’s (RA) role, although Bilal’s (RA) role remains intact
It confirms one person’s dream with another’s same dream
It changes the words of the adhan, although the words of the adhan remain unchanged
quiz.e: The same dream of the two supported each other.

quiz.q: When a new person comes to a religious work in the neighbourhood, how should he be welcomed; what can be learned from the adhan incident?
o: Giving responsibility only to the known, although Bilal (RA) too was new a day before
Giving no responsibility to newcomers, although responsibility was given to Bilal (RA)
Giving responsibility to the person of best ability (like Bilal (RA)), without looking at background, although ability was the criterion here
Deciding responsibility by lineage
quiz.e: Bilal (RA) was a slave until a day before.

quiz.q: In whose house did the Prophet ﷺ bind brotherhood between the Muhajirun and the Ansar?
o: The house of Anas ibn Malik (RA)
The house of Abu Ayyub (RA), where the Prophet ﷺ often sat
The house of Abu Bakr (RA), where he stayed the first night
The house of Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh (RA)
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 2294.

quiz.q: In answer to ‘Asim’s (RA) question, what did Anas (RA) say?
o: There is hilf in Islam, but only for war, which was said about later wars
The Prophet ﷺ made a bond between Quraysh and the Ansar in his very house
The Prophet ﷺ never made such a bond, although there is no such narration anywhere
This bond happened only after the conquest of Makkah
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 2294 (to the same effect 6083, 7340).

quiz.q: In the early bond of brotherhood of Muhajirun and Ansar, what rule of inheritance ran which was later abrogated?
o: No inheritance took effect at all, which is written nowhere in this chain
Only the Muhajirun would get the Ansar’s wealth
Instead of the blood relative, the person bound as brother would get the wealth
The entire wealth would become a donation for the mosque, which speaks of the financing of mosque building
quiz.e: Abrogated through Surah al-Anfal 75.

quiz.q: How does the bond of brotherhood of Muhajirun and Ansar differ from the old tribal ‘hilf’ of Arabia?
o: It was made only for war
It was limited only among the rich
It was invalid without any written document
It was not for blood or tribal interest
quiz.e: This difference is understood from Anas’s (RA) answer.

quiz.q: A new neighbour has come to the area; he knows no one. In the light of mu’akhah (making brotherhood), what should be done?
o: Leaving him as he is
Keeping distance from him
Standing by him
Ending the duty with only a salam
quiz.e: The bond of brotherhood of Muhajirun and Ansar teaches this.

quiz.q: With whom did the Prophet ﷺ bind Salman al-Farisi (RA) as brother?
o: Abu Bakr (RA)
Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ (RA)
Kharijah ibn Zayd (RA)
Abu al-Darda’ (RA)
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 1968.

quiz.q: What did Salman (RA) say to Abu al-Darda’ (RA)?
o: A right of the Lord, a right of oneself and a right of the family; each one who has a right must be given his right
The world must be left completely, although there is no such direct word in the hadith, which comes from a misunderstanding of tasawwuf
Fasting must never be broken, although the hadith speaks of fasting differently
Sleeping at night is forbidden, although it is the instruction to sleep that is in the hadith
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ said, Salman (RA) has spoken truly.

quiz.q: From the incident of Salman (RA) stopping Abu al-Darda’ (RA), which aspect of the bond of brotherhood is understood?
o: In the bond of brotherhood there was also the right to turn one another back from excess
In the bond of brotherhood commenting on each other’s worship is forbidden, although the Prophet ﷺ made no different comment
The bond of brotherhood was only for sharing wealth, although there was precedent of sharing wealth in the bond
The Prophet ﷺ had no role in the bond of brotherhood
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ confirmed Salman’s (RA) word as true.

quiz.q: A friend, going to excess in worship, is neglecting his health and family. From the incident of Salman (RA), what is to be done?
o: Encourage him to even more worship
Stay silent about him, it is his own matter
Leave him alone
Stop him out of love
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ said, Salman (RA) has spoken truly.

quiz.q: What did Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ (RA) propose to ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf (RA)?
o: Only showing the road to the market, which he had not actually wanted
Half the wealth and a marriage
Letting him stay in his house, although he had first stayed at Sa‘d’s (RA) house itself
Giving a she-camel as a gift, which was not by the Prophet’s ﷺ order
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 2049.

quiz.q: What did ‘Abd al-Rahman (RA) ask for in reply to that proposal?
o: All of the wealth
Permission to stay at Sa‘d’s (RA) house
Only the road to the market
A fellow trader
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 2049.

quiz.q: What did ‘Abd al-Rahman (RA) give as mahr in the marriage?
o: A goat, which the Prophet ﷺ mentioned for the walimah
Some ghee and cheese, which was the first earning in place of ghee and cheese
A camel, which was in Sa‘d’s first proposal
Gold the weight of a date stone
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ said, hold a walimah, even with a goat.

quiz.q: What did Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ (RA) do at ‘Abd al-Rahman’s (RA) refusal?
o: Angrily cut off the relationship, although he did not complain to the Prophet ﷺ
Did not insist; only showed the road to the market
Complained to the Prophet ﷺ, although he made no new proposal either
Made a new proposal again, although the relationship was intact
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 2049.

quiz.q: A friend, while helping, keeps reminding of that favour again and again. What can be learned from the story of Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ (RA)?
o: Help cannot be forced
It is better not to help
When taking help, expressing gratitude is forbidden
Help should be given only to the rich
quiz.e: Sa‘d (RA) did not insist even after half his wealth was refused.

quiz.q: Someone wants to start a business but has no capital. What can be learned from ‘Abd al-Rahman’s (RA) story?
o: A business should not be started without capital
One can start even with small capital (ghee and cheese)
First take everything from someone wealthy
One should not marry before business
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 2049.

porbos.title: Houses Were Allotted by Lot • The Muhajirun’s Hearts Wept • The Qur’anic Praise of the Ansar • The Night Guest • The Muhajirun’s Gratitude • A Sign of Faith • A Written Document • One Nation, Different Tribes • One Blood, One Judgement • The Neighbour Is Like Oneself

blocks.1: The Muhajirun were arriving one by one. Who would stay in whose house? Even in this question the Ansar did not apply their own preference. Which Ansari would take in which Muhajir, they settled by drawing lots.
blocks.3: The name of ‘Uthman ibn Maz‘un (RA) came up in the lottery to stay in our house, when the Ansar drew lots for the residence of the Muhajirun.{{1}}
blocks.4: No room was left for liking and disliking. Whoever fell to one’s lot became one’s guest. ‘Uthman ibn Maz‘un (RA) stayed in the house of Umm al-‘Ala’ (RA). When he fell ill, that Ansari woman nursed him, to the end.
blocks.6: A home was found, brothers were found. Still the houses of Makkah came to mind. After coming to Madinah, Abu Bakr (RA) and Bilal (RA) fell ill with fever. ‘A’ishah (RA) went to see them.
blocks.8: ‘A’ishah (RA) said: after the Prophet {{1}} came to Madinah, Abu Bakr (RA) and Bilal (RA) were seized by fever. I went to them and said, Father, how are you? Bilal, how are you? When the fever came on, Abu Bakr would say, every man is greeted in the morning among his family, while death is nearer to him than the strap of his sandal. And when the fever left Bilal he would raise his voice and say, Ah, if only I knew, shall I again spend a night in a valley around which will be idhkhir and jalil grass? Shall I again go down to the waters of Majinnah some day? Shall Shamah and Tafil mountains appear before me again? ‘A’ishah said, I went to the Prophet {{2}} and informed him. He said, O Allah, make Madinah as dear to us as we love Makkah, or even more. Make it healthy, bless us in its sa‘ and mudd, and move its fever to Juhfah.{{3}}
blocks.9: One was Bilal (RA), whose voice had said ‘Ahad’ under the whip in Makkah. That very man is now weeping for the grass of Makkah. The Prophet {{1}} did not scold them, nor belittle the memory. The love with which one loves Makkah, he asked the same for Madinah; even more.
blocks.10: The Qur’anic Praise of the Ansar
blocks.11: The Ansar were not alone like Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ (RA). This sharing was the habit of the whole Ansar community. Allah Himself sent down a verse about them.
blocks.13: And those who were already settled in this home (Madinah) and in faith before them, love whoever migrates to them, and feel no need in their hearts for what is given to them (that is, to the Muhajirun), and give them preference over themselves, even though they themselves are in want. In truth, those who are saved from the stinginess of their own selves, they are the successful.{{1}}
blocks.14: Putting others first even in one’s own want; the Qur’an has named this quality ‘ithar’. And it has called this one quality freedom from stinginess, and the key to success. So Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘’s (RA) offer of half his wealth was not a single event; it was the nature mixed into the blood of the whole Ansar community.
blocks.16: This verse is no imagined praise. It came in answer to a true event of one night. A man came to the Prophet {{1}} and said he was hungry. The Prophet {{2}} sent word to his wives’ houses. From every house the same answer came, there is nothing in the house but water.
blocks.18: Then the Messenger of Allah {{1}} said, who will host this one tonight? One of the Ansar said, I. He took the man to his wife and said, honour the guest of the Messenger of Allah {{2}}. The wife said, there is only the children’s food in the house. He said, set out the food, light the lamp, and if the children ask for supper, put them to sleep. The wife did so; she set out the food, lit the lamp, put the children to sleep. Then she got up, pretending to fix the lamp, and put it out. The two made the guest see as if they too were eating; yet that night they themselves passed without eating. In the morning that Ansari went to the Prophet {{3}}. The Prophet {{4}} said, tonight Allah laughed at the deed of you two, or said, was amazed. Then Allah sent down this verse, they give others preference over themselves even though they are in want.{{5}}
blocks.19: The lamp was put out so that the guest would not notice there was so little on the plate. Two people passed a night without eating. And in return came a verse of the Qur’an, which will be recited until the Day of Resurrection. Who that Ansari was, the narration has no name. The name was not kept written; the deed stayed written.
blocks.21: After all this a fear arose in the hearts of the Muhajirun. They came with this fear to the Prophet {{1}} himself.
blocks.23: When the Prophet {{1}} came to Madinah, the Muhajirun came to him and said, O Messenger of Allah, we have not seen a people who can give so much from plenty, nor be so sympathetic from little. Those among whom we have settled have borne the burden of our labour and made us share in their joy. We fear they will take away all the reward. The Prophet {{2}} said, no, as long as you pray to Allah for them and praise them.{{3}}
blocks.24: On one side the love of the Ansar. On the other the gratitude of the Muhajirun; not taking and staying silent, but returning it in du‘a and praise. The Prophet {{1}} gave both sides one task each. Those who received will pray. Those who gave, their reward is not reduced.
blocks.26: About the Ansar the Prophet {{1}} said one thing so briefly that it works like a measuring stick.
blocks.28: The sign of faith is love for the Ansar, and the sign of hypocrisy is hatred for the Ansar.{{1}}
blocks.29: Those who shared their house, land and food; love for them remained a sign of faith.
blocks.31: Brotherhood joined the houses. But when Muslims, Jews, and in their hearts doubtful people live together in one city, love alone does not suffice. The Prophet {{1}} had a document written. A charter; between the Muhajirun, the Ansar, and the Jewish tribes of Madinah.
blocks.32: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} wrote a document between the Muhajirun and the Ansar, in which he included the Jews too, kept them in their religion and wealth, and laid conditions on them, and laid conditions for them.{{2}}
blocks.33: The bond of brotherhood is a matter of the heart. But a city does not run on trust in the heart; there will be misunderstandings, quarrels, an outside enemy will come. So the Prophet {{1}} did not stop at oral understanding. This is no hadith; not an account from the mouth of any Companion. It is the verbatim text of a written document, which Ibn Ishaq has preserved in his Sirah book. Historians know it by the name ‘the Charter of Madinah’; it is counted as one of the first written constitutions of the world.{{2}}
blocks.34: Forty-seven clauses. In each clause a boundary drawn. Who will live with whom, who will give whom security, in a quarrel to whom to go.
blocks.36: The first word of the charter is the biggest declaration.
blocks.38: This written document is from Muhammad the unlettered Prophet, between the believers and Muslims of Quraysh and Yathrib, and those who follow them, join them and strive with them. Truly they are one nation, distinct from other people.{{1}}
blocks.39: The Muhajirun of Quraysh, the Ansar of Yathrib; different in tribe, different in lineage. But in this one line they became one nation. Then each tribe was written separately; Banu ‘Awf, Banu al-Harith, Banu Sa‘idah, Banu Jusham, Banu al-Najjar, Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf, Banu al-Nabit, Banu Aws. Each by its own old rules would bear one another’s blood-money, and share the cost of freeing captives fairly.{{1}}
blocks.40: The old tribal structure was not broken. Only a new roof was placed over it; the roof of justice. One clause states plainly,
blocks.42: And the believers shall not abandon among themselves one burdened by debt or crushed by the weight of many dependants; in the matter of ransom or blood-money, they shall give to him according to custom.{{1}}
blocks.43: If someone fell into debt, if someone fell into calamity, his tribe could not abandon him. This was the state’s first social security.
blocks.45: In the middle clauses of the charter, the matters of justice and security.
blocks.47: And no believer shall kill a believer for the sake of a disbeliever, nor help a disbeliever against a believer. And the protection of Allah is one; the lowest of them can give refuge. And the believers are friends of one another, to the exclusion of other people. And whoever of the Jews follows us shall have help and equal treatment; they shall not be wronged, nor shall anyone be helped against them. And the peace of the believers is one; in war in the way of Allah no believer shall make peace without the other believers, except on terms of equality and justice. And every party that goes out on an expedition with us shall relieve one another in turn. And in the blood shed in the way of Allah, the believers are equal sharers with one another; and the God-fearing believers are on the best and straightest path.{{1}}
blocks.48: The price of a believer’s life will not be measured by the tribe; no killing of a believer for a disbeliever’s interest, and in blood shed in the way of Allah all are equal sharers. And if a quarrel grew into a riot?
blocks.50: And in whatever matter you differ, its decision returns to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and to Muhammad.{{1}}
blocks.51: Not the personal wish of a tribal chief, not the strength of the sword; judgement would go to a fixed address. The way to stop the cycle of blood-revenge of Arabia is in this one line. Another clause tells for whom the city is safe, for whom not.
blocks.53: And it is not lawful for a believer who has affirmed what is in this document and believes in Allah and the Last Day, to help or shelter one who commits a new crime. And whoever helps or shelters him, upon him is the curse and wrath of Allah on the Day of Resurrection; from him no obligatory or voluntary act will be accepted.{{1}}
blocks.54: Shelter only for the innocent. To cover up a criminal is to stand against the whole charter.
blocks.56: One small clause of the charter almost escapes the eye, yet its weight is great.
blocks.58: And the neighbour is like oneself; not to be harmed, and not a sinner.{{1}}
blocks.59: The neighbour is like oneself; in this one comparison the whole responsibility is understood. I do not harm myself. Not harming the neighbour is to be just the same. The same thing the Prophet {{1}} said later in another way,
blocks.60: By Allah, he does not believe! By Allah, he does not believe! By Allah, he does not believe! It was asked, who, O Messenger of Allah? He said, the one whose neighbour is not safe from their harm.{{1}}
blocks.61: A word said with a threefold oath. The neighbour’s safety is the measure of faith.

footnotes.0: Sahih al-Bukhari 3929 (from Kharijah ibn Zayd ibn Thabit (RA), on the authority of Umm al-‘Ala’ (RA))
footnotes.2: Tawdih al-Qur’an (Mufti Muhammad Taqi ‘Uthmani), vol. 3, Surah al-Hashr 59:9, pp. 516–517 (translation: Tawdih al-Qur’an)
footnotes.3: Sahih al-Bukhari 3798 (from Abu Hurayrah (RA)); to the same effect Sahih Muslim 2054
footnotes.4: Jami‘ al-Tirmidhi 2487 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA); Imam al-Tirmidhi: hadithun sahihun hasanun gharib); to the same effect Sunan Abi Dawud 4812
footnotes.6: Ibn Ishaq, al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (in the narration of Ibn Hisham); Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Dustur al-Madinah’
footnotes.7: The nature and chain of the Charter of Madinah: it is not a saying narrated with a chain like a hadith, but the text of a written document preserved by Ibn Ishaq (d. 151 AH) in his Sirah book. Ibn Hisham compiled it from Ibn Ishaq. No manuscript of the original document survives; the text preserved by Ibn Ishaq is the only source. Most modern researchers regard its core content as historically reliable, since it bears no influence of the ideas current in later times. In this dars it is presented not as a hadith with a chain but as a document of the Sirah.

quiz.q: Which quality of the Ansar is praised in Surah al-Hashr 59:9?
o: Putting others before oneself even in one’s own want (ithar)
Showing bravery in war, which recalls the events of Badr and Uhud
Praying much at night, which recalls the prayer of the night of the Mi‘raj
Earning much wealth
quiz.e: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 3, Surah al-Hashr 59:9.

quiz.q: The phrase of the verse ‘those saved from stinginess are the successful’ matches which conduct of the Ansar?
o: ‘Abd al-Rahman’s (RA) going to the market, which speaks of seeking the road to the market
Salman’s (RA) fasting, which speaks of voluntary fasting worship
Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘’s (RA) offer of half the wealth
Bilal’s (RA) giving the adhan, which speaks of the first sound of the adhan
quiz.e: The verse was revealed in praise of the Ansar’s quality of ithar.

quiz.q: Someone helps a person in distress and then taunts them. In the light of Surah al-Hashr 59:9, how is this?
o: Not true ithar; a sign of not being freed from stinginess
This is natural, because the helper has a right
This matches the Ansar’s way, although the Ansar truly showed this quality
The reward increases by it, although the promise of reward is in the verse in a different way
quiz.e: In the verse freedom from stinginess itself is called success.

quiz.q: What exactly is the Charter of Madinah?
o: A hadith, narrated directly with a chain from a Companion
The text of a written document preserved in Ibn Ishaq’s Sirah book
A verse of the Qur’an, although it has no continuity of chain
A summary of the Prophet’s ﷺ oral speech, although it was written in Arabic itself
quiz.e: Not a hadith from the mouth of any Companion, but the verbatim text of a document.

quiz.q: Why is the Charter of Madinah called a ‘document’ rather than a ‘hadith’?
o: Because it is part of the Qur’an, although the sentences of the charter begin in the name of the Prophet ﷺ
Because no Companion wrote it, although many rulings of the Qur’an were being revealed at the same time
Because it is not written in Arabic
Because it is not a saying narrated with a chain, but a written text preserved by Ibn Ishaq
quiz.e: This distinction between hadith and document is important for verification.

quiz.q: An organisation has no written rules, only oral understanding. What can be learned from the Charter of Madinah?
o: Oral understanding is enough, although oral understanding is also a kind of promise
Written rules are a sign of distrust, although the Charter of Madinah itself was made in writing
Having no rules is freedom
To make a written document instead of stopping at oral understanding
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ did not stop at a word of promise; he had it written.

quiz.q: What is declared in the first clause of the Charter of Madinah?
o: Only Muslims can live in Madinah, although the charter included the Jews too
Each tribe will be counted as a separate state
The Muhajirun and Ansar are one nation distinct from all other people
No dispute can be settled without war, although the old rules of each tribe were kept
quiz.e: Dustur al-Madinah, clause 1.

quiz.q: According to the charter, what happens if a believer falls into debt?
o: They will be expelled from the tribe
Their wealth will be confiscated, which is written nowhere in the charter
They must repay the debt alone, which speaks only of the ransom of war captives
The believers will not deprive them of giving, according to custom
quiz.e: Dustur al-Madinah, clause 11.

quiz.q: How was the old tribal structure used in the charter?
o: The tribal structure was not broken
All tribes were broken to make one tribe
The power of tribal chiefs was increased
Competition between tribes was encouraged
quiz.e: In clauses 2–10 the old rules of each tribe were kept.

quiz.q: According to the charter, where should one go to settle a dispute?
o: To Allah and Muhammad ﷺ
To the tribal chief, which is in no clause of the charter
To the richest person, which would have created dependence on a neighbouring tribe
To the arbitration of a neighbouring tribe
quiz.e: Dustur al-Madinah, clause 23.

quiz.q: What does the charter say about killing a believer?
o: The punishment for killing a rich believer will be greater, which is not in the charter
No believer will kill another believer for the sake of a disbeliever
Only the killing of the Ansar will be judged, which is not in the charter
Rules of killing will differ by tribe, which is not in the charter
quiz.e: Dustur al-Madinah, clauses 14, 19.

quiz.q: Why is the condition of ‘returning to Allah and Muhammad ﷺ’ for settling a dispute important?
o: It shows that judgement always went in the Prophet’s ﷺ favour, although that was exactly what was customary in the pre-Islamic era
It speaks of judgement going to a fixed address instead of the tribal chief’s wish or the sword
It increases the power of tribal chiefs, which would have reduced the power of tribal chiefs
It increases war further, although in reality that often happened
quiz.e: A step toward stopping the cycle of blood-revenge of Arabia.

quiz.q: In an area, people go to fighting to settle a dispute. Which clause of the Charter of Madinah can be applied?
o: Returning the dispute to Allah and His Messenger (today, the principles of the din), which is a path opposite to the principle of the charter
Accepting the word of the stronger party, which is a method opposite to clause 23 of the charter
Avoiding the dispute, which is a method opposite to clause 23 of the charter
Each judging for themselves
quiz.e: Clause 23.

quiz.q: What does the Charter of Madinah say about the neighbour?
o: The neighbour has a right in one’s wealth
The neighbour must always be given food
The neighbour is like oneself
There is no instruction about the neighbour
quiz.e: Dustur al-Madinah, clause 40.

quiz.q: Saying ‘By Allah, he does not believe’ three times, whom did the Prophet ﷺ speak of?
o: One who does not pray, although there is a different hadith about prayer
One who does not fast, although there is a different hadith about fasting
One who does not give zakat, although there is a different hadith about zakat
The one whose neighbour is not safe from their harm
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 6016.

quiz.q: What do the clause ‘the neighbour is like oneself’ and the hadith ‘one whose neighbour is not safe does not believe’ show together?
o: The two are opposed to each other, although both are in fact true claims
The hadith was added after the charter
The written law and the Prophet’s ﷺ word give the same message in two ways
Only the Muslim neighbour is spoken of, although the hadith speaks of all neighbours
quiz.e: The same value has come in the law and in the hadith in two ways.

quiz.q: A person is indifferent to their neighbour’s distress. Combining the Charter of Madinah and the hadith, what can be said to them?
o: The neighbour’s distress is the neighbour’s own responsibility
It is better to keep no relation with the neighbour
There is no guidance in Islam about the neighbour
The neighbour is like oneself
quiz.e: Dustur al-Madinah clause 40 and Sahih al-Bukhari 6016.

porbos.title: In the Same Charter with the Jews • The Charter’s Final Word • The Charter of Madinah: Full Text • The Road to the Market • One Body • Our Home Today • Final Word

blocks.0: In the Same Charter with the Jews
blocks.1: Many clauses of the charter are about the Jews.
blocks.3: And truly the Jews of Banu ‘Awf are one nation with the believers; for the Jews their din, for the Muslims their din; and so for their allies and for themselves.{{1}}
blocks.4: Part of one nation, but keeping religion separate. No condition of forcibly changing din is here. This same thing was written in separate clauses for the Jews of Banu al-Najjar, Banu al-Harith, Banu Sa‘idah, Banu Jusham, Banu Aws, Banu Tha‘labah.{{1}}
blocks.5: The share of expenses was stated separately too.
blocks.7: And truly the expenses of the Jews are on the Jews, the expenses of the Muslims on the Muslims. And whoever fights against the parties of this document, there will be mutual help among them against that one. And among them will be well-wishing and good counsel, and righteousness; not sin.{{1}}
blocks.8: And in the defence of the city?
blocks.10: And truly whatever event or dispute occurs among the parties of this document, of which corruption is feared, its decision returns to Allah and the Messenger of Allah, Muhammad. And Allah is witness to the most God-fearing and most righteous part of this document. And truly Quraysh and those who help them will not be given refuge. And whoever attacks Yathrib, there will be mutual help among them against that one.{{1}}
blocks.11: The city now belonged to all. If an outsider attacked, Jew and Muslim would stand together. Historians call this one of the first written constitutions of the world. Here no one’s religion was taken away; only the rules for living in one city were written.
blocks.13: At the end of the forty-seven clauses, a general declaration.
blocks.15: No earner earns except against himself. And truly Allah is witness to the truest and most righteous part of this document. And truly this writing will not be a barrier for an oppressor or a sinner. And truly whoever goes out is safe, and whoever stays in Madinah is safe; except one who has wronged and sinned. And truly Allah is the neighbour-protector of the one who does good and keeps taqwa. And Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.{{1}}
blocks.16: A state ends with these words; security for everyone, only not for the oppressor. Nowhere in this document is it written that anyone must change religion. What is written is only who is whose neighbour, who will take responsibility for whom, to whom to go in a quarrel. That a city can hold many kinds of people, this one writing is its proof.
blocks.17: The Charter of Madinah: Full Text
blocks.18: Many clauses of the charter have come until now in pieces. Now the whole text, in the charter’s own words, in the order of the clauses. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. This written document is from Muhammad the unlettered Prophet, between the believers and Muslims of Quraysh and Yathrib, and those who follow them, join them and strive with them. 1. Truly they are one nation, distinct from other people. 2. The Muhajirun of Quraysh will remain on their former custom; they will bear blood-money among themselves, and ransom their captives by the custom and fairness current among the believers. 3. And Banu ‘Awf will remain on their former custom; they will bear blood-money by the old rule, and every party will ransom its captives by the custom and fairness current among the believers. 4. And Banu al-Harith will remain on their former custom, as in the third clause. 5. And Banu Sa‘idah will remain on their former custom, as in the third clause. 6. And Banu Jusham will remain on their former custom, as in the third clause. 7. And Banu al-Najjar will remain on their former custom, as in the third clause. 8. And Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf will remain on their former custom, as in the third clause. 9. And Banu al-Nabit will remain on their former custom, as in the third clause. 10. And Banu Aws will remain on their former custom, as in the third clause. 11. And the believers shall not abandon among themselves one bent under debt or distressed by the burden of many dependants; in the matter of ransom or blood-money, they shall give to him according to custom. 12. And no believer shall make a pact with the freed ally of another believer, excluding him (his master). 13. And the God-fearing believers will be against the one among them who transgresses or seeks any scheme of injustice, sin, enmity or corruption among the believers; all their hands will be on him, even if he is the child of one of them. 14. And no believer shall kill a believer for the sake of a disbeliever, nor help a disbeliever against a believer. 15. And truly the protection of Allah is one; the lowest of them can give refuge. And the believers are friends of one another, to the exclusion of other people. 16. And whoever of the Jews follows us shall have help and equal treatment; he will not be wronged, nor will anyone be helped against him. 17. And the peace of the believers is one; in war in the way of Allah no believer shall make peace without the other believers, except on terms of equality and fairness. 18. And every party that goes out on an expedition with us shall relieve one another in turn. 19. And in the blood shed in the way of Allah, the believers are equal sharers with one another; and the God-fearing believers are on the best and straightest path. 20. And no polytheist shall give refuge to the property or life of Quraysh, nor stand as a barrier on his behalf against any believer. 21. And whoever kills a believer wrongfully, with proof, shall be subject to retaliation, unless the guardian of the slain is satisfied. All the believers are against him; nothing is lawful for them except standing against him. 22. And truly it is not lawful for a believer who has affirmed what is in this document and believes in Allah and the Day of Resurrection to help or shelter one who commits a new crime. Whoever helps or shelters him, upon him is the curse and wrath of Allah on the Day of Resurrection; from him no obligatory or voluntary act will be accepted. 23. And in whatever matter you differ, its decision returns to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and to Muhammad {{1}}. 24. And the Jews will bear the expense with the believers, as long as they are at war. 25. And the Jews of Banu ‘Awf are one nation with the believers; for the Jews their din, for the Muslims their din; and so for their allies and for themselves. But whoever wrongs and sins will destroy only himself and his family. 26. And for the Jews of Banu al-Najjar, the same as for the Jews of Banu ‘Awf. 27. And for the Jews of Banu al-Harith, the same as for the Jews of Banu ‘Awf. 28. And for the Jews of Banu Sa‘idah, the same as for the Jews of Banu ‘Awf. 29. And for the Jews of Banu Jusham, the same as for the Jews of Banu ‘Awf. 30. And for the Jews of Banu Aws, the same as for the Jews of Banu ‘Awf. 31. And for the Jews of Banu Tha‘labah, the same as for the Jews of Banu ‘Awf; but whoever wrongs and sins will destroy only himself and his family. 32. And Jafnah, a branch of Tha‘labah, are like themselves. 33. And for Banu Shutaybah, the same as for the Jews of Banu ‘Awf; and righteousness, not sin. 34. And the allies of Tha‘labah are like themselves. 35. And the close associates of the Jews are like themselves. 36. And none of them will go out (to war) without the permission of Muhammad. There will be no barrier on the path of retaliation for a wound. Whoever attacks suddenly will bring it upon himself and his family, unless he is wronged. Allah is witness to the most righteous part of this matter. 37. And the expenses of the Jews are on the Jews, the expenses of the Muslims on the Muslims. Whoever fights against the parties of this document, there will be mutual help among them against him. Among them will be well-wishing and good counsel, and righteousness; not sin. No one will be sinful because of his ally. And help is for the wronged. 38. And the Jews will bear the expense with the believers, as long as they are at war. 39. And the interior of Yathrib is sacred, forbidden ground, for the parties of this document. 40. And the neighbour is like oneself; he is not to be harmed, nor is he sinful. 41. And no honoured protected person shall be given refuge without the permission of his guardians. 42. And whatever event or dispute occurs among the parties of this document, of which corruption is feared, its decision returns to Allah and the Messenger of Allah, Muhammad {{2}}. Allah is witness to the most God-fearing and most righteous part of this document. 43. And Quraysh and those who help them will not be given refuge. 44. And whoever attacks Yathrib, there will be mutual help among them against him. 45. And if they are called to peace, they will make peace and accept it. If the believers too are called likewise, it will bind the believers too, except one who fights against the din. Each group’s share is for its own side. 46. And the Jews of Aws, their allies and themselves, will be in the same rights as the parties of this document, with good treatment from the parties of this document; and righteousness, not sin. 47. No earner earns except against himself. Allah is witness to the truest and most righteous part of this document. This writing will not be a barrier for an oppressor or a sinner. Whoever goes out is safe, and whoever stays in Madinah is safe; except one who has wronged and sinned. Allah is the neighbour-protector of the one who does good and keeps taqwa. And Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah {{3}}.{{4}}
blocks.20: ‘Abd al-Rahman (RA) asked for the road to the market. That market too the Prophet {{1}} himself had fixed. In one narration he looked at the market of the Nabit (the Nabataean people), and said, this is not your market. He looked at another market, that too did not please. Coming back from a third place he said,
blocks.22: This is your market. Here no place will be assigned, and no tax will be imposed on it.{{1}}
blocks.23: The chain is weak, so this cannot be taken as evidence. Only as a scene; that Madinah had an open, tax-free market, this much is supported by other narrations and history too. On the road to that market ‘Abd al-Rahman (RA) walked. Not anyone’s mercy; the earning of his own hands.
blocks.25: The charter makes brothers on paper. But the Prophet {{1}} wanted the bond to descend into the heart too. So he kept saying the same thing in different ways.
blocks.26: The believers, in mutual mercy, love and compassion, are like one body; when any limb of the body hurts, the whole body stays awake, shivering with fever.{{1}}
blocks.27: When one hurts, the whole body is awake. Through the pain of one, the whole society is meant to be stirred. Another time he interlaced his fingers one with another and showed.
blocks.28: A believer is to another believer like a wall; each holds the other firmly. Saying this, he interlaced his fingers together and showed.{{1}}
blocks.29: A brick does not stand alone. The brick beside it holds it up. And the smallest, hardest measure he said in one sentence.
blocks.30: None of you will be a believer until he likes for his brother what he likes for himself.{{1}}
blocks.31: What I want for myself, the same for my brother. With this one measure one can check oneself every day.
blocks.33: This forming of the state at Madinah returns to our home today at several places. The first place is the manner of helping. Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ (RA) wished to give half his wealth. ‘Abd al-Rahman (RA) did not take it; he took only the road to the market. Sa‘d did not insist either; he showed the road and stopped. Today when we go to help someone we often make them small. In the manner of alms, reminding again and again of the favour. When a person is made small in taking help, the fault is the giver’s. There is a dignified manner of giving; learning it is important.
blocks.34: The second place is that of one body. When calamity comes in a neighbour’s house, do we shiver with fever, or just ask for news and finish? The third place is that of the written document. The Prophet {{1}} did not stop at an oral promise; he had it written, so that no one could later deny. The understandings in our families and institutions that remain oral, how many take the form of writing?
blocks.35: The fourth place is that of one nation within difference. In the Charter of Madinah, Muslims and Jews in the same city, under the same charter, yet to each their own religion. Today around us too there are people of other views; neighbours, colleagues, relatives. The city is everyone’s, the rule is meant to be just for everyone.
blocks.36: The fifth place is that of the right to correct. Salman (RA) stopped Abu al-Darda’ (RA), and the Prophet {{1}} endorsed it. Today, seeing the excess of a friend or brother, do we have the courage to stop them, or do we stay silent and save the relationship?
blocks.37: The sixth place is the neighbour’s. ‘The neighbour is like oneself’; this one line of the Charter of Madinah. Today do we know the name of the person in the next flat, the next house? The seventh place is the night guest. Putting out the lamp, that Ansari couple passed the night without eating. The guest did not even understand. Today when we feed someone we announce it on social media. The one whose name did not even remain in history, his sacrifice is the deepest.
blocks.38: The eighth place is the date-orchard proposal. The Ansar had wanted to give away the land; the Prophet {{1}} did not agree and chose the exchange for labour. Today, helping someone, we often think donating is the greatest gift. Yet a task, a partnership, an opportunity; these too are help of equal worth, and keep someone’s self-respect intact even more.
blocks.39: The ninth place is not spreading word without verifying. Even in the single question of whose brother the Prophet {{1}} himself was, Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Kathir remained careful; where there is no chain, they said plainly there is no chain. Today we spread what we hear about beloved people and beloved leaders without verifying. Spreading a wrong piece of information even in the name of love is wrong; however great the person concerned may be.
blocks.40: The tenth place is gratitude. The Muhajirun, having received so much, were still afraid: has all the reward gone to them? The Prophet {{1}} showed the way, du‘a and praise. Today we take a favour from someone and either forget it or consider it a burden. When did we last pray from the heart for someone?
blocks.42: In today’s dars we saw how a city became a state. One call; the adhan, first uttered through the voice of a slave of not long before. One bond; the brotherhood of Muhajirun and Ansar, where instead of half the wealth someone asked only for a road. One writing; the Charter of Madinah, where Muslims and Jews in the same city, under the same law, yet each in their own religion.
blocks.43: The manner of Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ (RA) is the lesson of this dars. He wished to give half his wealth, but when ‘Abd al-Rahman (RA) asked only for the road, he did not insist. The giving hand must always be kept wide, but no one has the right to make the taking hand small. That breadth of Sa‘d, Allah Himself sealed in Surah al-Hashr; putting others first even in one’s own want. In the next dars we will see how the qiblah changed in this new state, and how the rulings came step by step.
blocks.44: So take one deed with you from today’s dars.
blocks.46: The Ansari brother wished to give half the wealth; the Muhajir brother took only the road to the market, and between the two there was no being made small. Today I will ask myself a question: when I help someone, does their self-respect get a scratch?
blocks.47: Today I will help someone by showing just a way, not by donating; which I will not leave from today on.

quiz.q: What does the charter say about the Jews of Banu ‘Awf?
o: They are one nation with the believers; for the Jews their religion, for the Muslims their religion
They must leave Madinah, which is in no clause of the charter, which is in no clause of the charter at all
They must accept Islam, which is contrary to the charter’s main aim
They will have no rights, which is contrary to the charter’s last clause
quiz.e: Dustur al-Madinah, clause 25.

quiz.q: According to the charter, what will the Jews and Muslims do in the defence of Madinah?
o: Each defend their own area separately, which is contrary to the charter’s idea of joint defence
Help one another if the partners of the charter are attacked
Only the Muslims will take the responsibility of defence, which is contrary to the charter’s clause of being one nation
When an external enemy comes the Jews will leave the city
quiz.e: Dustur al-Madinah, clauses 39, 44.

quiz.q: What does the principle of ‘one nation, different religions’ in the charter with the Jews show?
o: The Jews too must pray
The Jews will be subject citizens under the Muslims
The Jews have no right to property
Partners in civil rights
quiz.e: In clauses 25–35 the same thing is repeated.

quiz.q: In an institution, workers of different faiths work together. Which principle of the Charter of Madinah can be applied?
o: Asking everyone to follow the same religion, which is a method contrary to the main aim of the charter
The same rules for all, but no interference in anyone’s religion
Giving the people of different faiths separate rules, which is a method contrary to the main aim of the charter
Excluding the people of different faiths
quiz.e: Clause 25: for the Jews their religion, for the Muslims their religion.

quiz.q: If people of another religion in an area are attacked, what should Muslim neighbours do, in the light of the charter?
o: Look only to their own security, although the charter speaks of joint defence
Stand beside them as partners of the charter
Stay away from the event, although the charter speaks of joint defence
Just pray and sit
quiz.e: Clauses 39, 44: the pledge of mutual defence.

quiz.q: In the last clause of the Charter of Madinah, whom was security not given?
o: Those who leave Madinah
Those who do business
Those who oppress or commit sin
Those who keep relations with another tribe
quiz.e: Dustur al-Madinah, clause 47.

quiz.q: What is the meaning of ‘the one who goes out is safe, the one who stays is safe’ in the last clause?
o: Security is for everyone except the oppressor and the criminal
Leaving the city means no protection, although there is no such opposite statement in the clause
Only those who go to war are safe, although there is no such opposite statement in the clause
Security is only for the rich
quiz.e: Clause 47.

quiz.q: What did ‘Abd al-Rahman (RA) first bring back from the market?
o: A date stone of gold
A goat
A bolt of cloth
Ghee and cheese

quiz.q: In one weak narration, what did the Prophet ﷺ say about the market of Madinah?

In this market only Muslims will trade
In this market the prices of all goods will be fixed
This market will be closed on Friday

quiz.q: What do ‘Abd al-Rahman’s (RA) asking for the road to the market and the tax-free market of the weak narration show together?

In Madinah there was an opportunity of one’s own earning instead of anyone’s mercy
